description: Apply database optimistic concurrency control principles to parallel DEFLATE decompression. Multiple decoder threads work on different segments of a block simultaneously without locks. Each thread speculatively decodes its segment. At merge time, validate that each thread's starting state was correct. If not, re-execute only the invalidated segments - analogous to transaction abort and retry.
mathematical_formalization: N threads, each processes segment of size B/N bits. Thread i starts speculatively from guessed offset o_i. Validation: check if thread_{i-1}'s final offset equals o_i. If yes, commit; if no, abort and re-execute from correct offset. Expected re-executions E[R] = N * P(sync_fail). Total time T = max(B/(N*throughput), R * B/(N*throughput)). Beneficial when P(sync_fail) < (N-1)/N.
analogical_connections: Optimistic concurrency control in databases: process transactions, validate at commit time
Speculative multithreading in compilers: execute loop iterations in parallel, validate dependencies
Map-reduce: map phase is speculative, reduce phase validates and merges
implementation_hypothesis: Divide DEFLATE block into N segments at estimated bit boundaries. Each thread: (1) find sync point using concept 002, (2) decode Huffman symbols from sync point to estimated end, (3) write decoded symbols to a temporary buffer. Main thread: validate segment boundaries match, concatenate output buffers, then run LZ77 reconstruction serially (or with concept 004 SIMD copies). Retry any failed segments.
experiment_seed: Implement 2-thread optimistic decode for large DEFLATE blocks (>32KB). Measure sync-finding overhead, decode parallelism, and validation/retry rate. Compare total throughput against single-thread decode on 4+ core machine. Target: 1.5x throughput with 2 threads for large blocks.
